action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right frontoparietal 5.8 cm mass at the precentral and superior frontal gyri extending into the corona radiata, with thick irregular ring enhancement, central necrosis, intratumoral hemorrhage, rim restricted diffusion, subfalcine herniation and 8 mm leftward midline shift
action_criteria.label: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol with DWI, FLAIR, post-contrast T1) to characterize the right frontoparietal lesion, define mass effect, and plan surgery
action_criteria.rationale: Contrast MRI with diffusion and FLAIR characterizes the lesion and its mass effect, identifies the enhancing target and plans the surgical approach (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Maximum rCBV ratio 4.8 in the posterior-medial enhancing rim with an avascular necrotic core, supporting a high-grade neoplasm and targeting sampling
action_criteria.label: Order MR perfusion imaging (DSC perfusion) to assess tumor vascularity and target highest-grade region for biopsy
action_criteria.rationale: Perfusion supports a high-grade neoplasm and identifies the most vascular region to sample; tissue decides the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Cho/NAA 5.2 with lipid-lactate in the enhancing rim and mildly raised choline in the peritumoral FLAIR region
action_criteria.label: Order MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to characterize tumor metabolic profile
action_criteria.rationale: Spectroscopy supports a high-grade neoplasm and shows infiltration beyond the enhancing margin; tissue decides the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No extracranial primary malignancy identified, supporting primary brain tumor as the working diagnosis
action_criteria.label: Order CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as staging to exclude an extracranial primary if a solitary metastasis is on the differential
action_criteria.rationale: A former smoker aged 71 with a family history of lung cancer: staging CT excludes an extracranial primary if a solitary metastasis is considered.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Glucose 151 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.3% in known type 2 diabetes, relevant to dexamethasone; electrolytes, platelets and coagulation normal: no laboratory contraindication to surgery
action_criteria.label: Order pre-operative laboratory workup: CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel, coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT), and type & screen in anticipation of surgical biopsy/resection
action_criteria.rationale: Surgery and corticosteroids are planned; coagulation, platelets, electrolytes, glucose and a group and screen are needed first.

action_criteria.label: Score performance status (Karnofsky and ECOG) at this visit
action_criteria.rationale: The choice between standard and hypofractionated chemoradiotherapy depends on age and Karnofsky performance status (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right hand motor area displaced about 6 mm from the enhancing margin, supplementary motor area about 4 mm from it; left-hemisphere language dominance
action_criteria.label: Order functional MRI (motor and language mapping) before resection of the right frontoparietal tumor at the precentral gyrus
action_criteria.rationale: The tumor is centered at the precentral and superior frontal gyri; motor and SMA mapping defines the resection margin (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right corticospinal tract continuous about 5 mm from the enhancing margin; right optic radiation continuous through the edematous parietal white matter
action_criteria.label: Order DTI tractography of the right corticospinal tract and optic radiation before resection
action_criteria.rationale: The tumor extends into the corona radiata and the parietal edema involves the optic radiation (left hemianopia); tractography locates both (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Integrated diagnosis Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4 with IDH1 R132H negative, ATRX retained, MGMT promoter methylated
action_criteria.label: Obtain tissue by maximal safe resection of the right frontoparietal lesion, or stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible, for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis with IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry, ATRX immunohistochemistry and MGMT promoter methylation
action_criteria.rationale: Surgery is the first option for a resectable glioma and should be as extensive as safely possible (AIOM; EANO 2021). Only tissue establishes the integrated diagnosis and the molecular results that select treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Steroid hyperglycemia on metformin and steroid plus aspirin GI risk identified; levetiracetam free of relevant interactions
action_criteria.label: Check interactions of dexamethasone and levetiracetam with the current medicines (metformin, aspirin, amlodipine, rosuvastatin, tamsulosin)
action_criteria.rationale: Dexamethasone worsens glycemic control and adds GI bleeding risk with aspirin; enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs are avoided.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform lumbar puncture: the 8 mm midline shift with subfalcine herniation and bilateral papilledema create a risk of herniation.
Do not initiate definitive tumor-directed therapy (radiation, temozolomide, alkylating chemotherapy) before tissue diagnosis is established
Do not start therapeutic anticoagulation without a clear thromboembolic indication, given upcoming neurosurgical intervention and bleeding risk
required_recommendations: Refer urgently to neurosurgery for maximal safe resection of the right frontoparietal lesion, with preoperative functional MRI and DTI tractography and intraoperative mapping, with stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible; send the specimen for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis (WHO CNS5).

Start dexamethasone for symptomatic vasogenic edema (for example 4 mg every 6 to 8 hours after a loading dose when mass effect is marked) at the lowest effective dose, with glucose monitoring and gastric protection, and taper after surgery.

Start antiseizure treatment with levetiracetam for the documented seizure with bilateral tonic-clonic activity and postictal left-sided weakness; this is treatment of tumor-related epilepsy, not prophylaxis. Avoid enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital), which lower dexamethasone and chemotherapy exposure.
Stop primary-prevention aspirin and over-the-counter ibuprofen before neurosurgery and while on dexamethasone (platelet effect and GI bleeding).
Monitor capillary glucose at least every 6 hours on dexamethasone and adjust the antihyperglycemic regimen (metformin, adding insulin if needed), given type 2 diabetes with HbA1c 7.3%.

After the integrated diagnosis, refer to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary team; for glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype over age 70 with MGMT promoter methylation, hypofractionated radiotherapy (40 Gy in 15 fractions) with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide, or temozolomide alone if radiotherapy is not tolerated (EANO 2021).

differential.key_features: Former smoker aged 71 with a family history of lung cancer, but no known primary; staging CT chest, abdomen and pelvis negative; a single infiltrative mass favors a primary glioma; tissue shows a glial neoplasm

key_clinical_evidence: Three weeks of morning headache, left hand weakness, a left visual field deficit and a first seizure at 71 call for urgent contrast-enhanced brain MRI

The MRI shows a right frontoparietal mass with thick irregular ring enhancement, central necrosis, hemorrhage, rim restricted diffusion and 8 mm midline shift with subfalcine herniation: a high-grade neoplasm on imaging
Perfusion (rCBV 4.8) and spectroscopy (Cho/NAA 5.2, lipid-lactate) support a high-grade neoplasm and target sampling; they do not grade the tumor
Bilateral papilledema and subfalcine herniation: dexamethasone, and lumbar puncture is contraindicated
Only tissue gives the integrated diagnosis: IDH1 R132H negative at 71, ATRX retained, with microvascular proliferation and necrosis, is glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4; MGMT is methylated
Age over 70: after surgery the standard is hypofractionated radiotherapy (40 Gy in 15 fractions) with temozolomide, chosen with the KPS (70) and the methylated MGMT, not the 60 Gy Stupp schedule
The tumor abuts the hand motor area and SMA and the edema involves the optic radiation, so functional MRI and DTI plan the resection
A seizure with postictal left-sided weakness is tumor-related epilepsy: levetiracetam is treatment, not prophylaxis, and enzyme-inducing drugs are avoided

clinical_pearls: Glioblastoma is the most common and most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults, with median survival of 14-16 months with standard treatment
The Stupp protocol (surgical resection followed by 6 weeks concurrent temozolomide/radiation then 6 cycles adjuvant temozolomide) remains the standard of care
MGMT promoter methylation is present in approximately 40-45% of glioblastomas and is associated with improved survival with temozolomide therapy
New-onset seizure in an adult over 40 should always raise suspicion for a brain tumor until proven otherwise

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Kenji Watanabe is a 71-year-old right-handed retired mathematics teacher who presents to the emergency department after experiencing a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home approximately two hours ago. His wife reports that over the past three weeks he has been complaining of progressively worsening right-sided headaches that are worst in the morning upon waking and occasionally awaken him from sleep. He initially attributed these to tension headaches and self-treated with over-the-counter ibuprofen with only partial relief. Over the past ten days, she has noticed increasing difficulty with his left hand: he has been dropping objects, had trouble buttoning his shirt, and his handwriting has become noticeably clumsier. She also reports subtle personality changes over the past two weeks, describing him as more irritable and less engaged in conversation than usual. Three days ago he began complaining of intermittent blurry vision, particularly in his left visual field, noting he bumped into a doorframe on his left side. This morning, while eating breakfast, his wife witnessed him suddenly stiffen, drop his fork, and fall from his chair onto the floor with rhythmic jerking of all four extremities lasting approximately 90 seconds. He was briefly unresponsive afterward and gradually became confused and drowsy. EMS was called and upon their arrival approximately 10 minutes later, he was postictal with slurred speech and marked left-sided weakness. He was transported to the emergency department where he has gradually become more alert over the past hour. He has no prior history of seizures. He denies recent head trauma, fever, neck stiffness, or weight loss, although his wife notes his appetite has been reduced over the past two weeks and he may have lost a few pounds.
